claims.text: High configurational entropy and severe local lattice distortion jointly govern the elevated-temperature structural evolution of nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal HENA nanoparticles.
Configurational entropy and lattice distortion create a sluggish-diffusion regime in these nanoparticles.
Sluggish diffusion significantly retards grain growth relative to traditional binary or ternary alloys.
Sluggish diffusion significantly retards atomic intermixing relative to traditional binary or ternary alloys.
Traditional alloys exhibit classical Arrhenius grain-growth kinetics with comparatively high diffusion coefficients.
HENA grain growth is non-monotonic, with rapid initial coarsening followed by a drastic slowdown.
The initial coarsening phase is driven by reduction of surface energy.
After roughly 100 hours, the particles approach a structurally stable, low-growth-rate state.
Traditional-alloy stability is often produced by second-phase Zener pinning rather than intrinsic kinetic hindrance.
Atomic-size mismatch and chemical complexity create a rugged potential-energy landscape that raises the activation energy for diffusion.
The resulting kinetic barrier suppresses grain-boundary migration.
The resulting kinetic barrier suppresses atomic interdiffusion.
Nanoparticle stabilization is intrinsic and does not depend on external pinning phases.
The stabilized grain-growth rate will be below 0.001 micrometres per hour.
At 1000 °C, diffusion coefficients will be below 10^-19 square metres per second.
The single-phase solid solution will persist to temperatures approaching the melting point without significant phase separation or precipitation during the test.
Below approximately 2 nm, surface diffusion can dominate and bypass the lattice-distortion barrier.
Large deviations from equiatomic composition reduce the configurational-entropy contribution and can promote phase separation.
Exceeding the melting point of the lowest-melting constituent causes melting and removes the solid-state diffusion barrier.
Surface oxidation can alter the operative diffusion pathway.

contradictions.description: The stated boundary conditions require an initial particle diameter below 10 nm, whereas the falsification experiment includes 10 nm and 20 nm particles.
